first_impression.reaction: Our daughter sent this. Bali at least feels closer to home than some places she's mentioned. The opening is sensible: pick the area, then the venue, and it's written plainly with no silly slang. I read it all on the iPad, but fifteen venues is a lot, and by the middle I was skimming the lists. 'Not published' comes up again and again. I liked the practical parts: the 90 minutes from the airport, the rest day, the branded alcohol warning, the emergency numbers. But nowhere does it talk about deposits, contracts or travel insurance. And it never says whether Mum, with her walking frame, can get to a clifftop chapel.

journey.quote: The right one depends on how many guests are flying in, the ceremony you want and the setting you want behind you as you say your vows.
journey.reaction: Good. It starts with the guests, not just the view. That's the right way round.

journey.quote: Bali's wet season usually runs from around October to April, and Smartraveller advises a high degree of caution in Indonesia, so build weather and travel fallbacks into your plans.
journey.reaction: Honest, and it quotes the government. I'd rather know this now than find out on the day.

journey.quote: A 60-guest ceremony fits Tresna Chapel, but a seated dinner for the same group needs a second space, so plan the move between them into the timeline.
journey.reaction: Move between them how? Up and down a cliff? My mother uses a walking frame. Is there a path or a buggy, or is it all steps?

journey.quote: Not published: capacity, room count, exclusive use.
journey.reaction: By now I've read 'Not published' many times. I understand they're being careful, but fifteen venues of bullet points is heavy going, and I've started skimming.

journey.quote: Site visits are by appointment, and whether a minimum spend or rental fee applies depends on the space and the type of event.
journey.reaction: So I still don't know if we're talking tens of thousands or more. Not even a rough 'From AUD' anywhere. Geoff will ask that first.

journey.quote: The resort is 90 minutes by car from Ngurah Rai International Airport, so build a rest gap into the arrival day.
journey.reaction: Very sensible. Someone has thought about the older ones arriving tired.

journey.section: Guest count, rooms and exclusive use
journey.quote: your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you sign
journey.reaction: In writing, before signing. That's what I want to hear with our money.

journey.section: How do guests get to Bali and between the areas?
journey.quote: Damaged passports, including water damage or minor tears, have led to refused entry, so ask guests to check theirs early.
journey.reaction: I'd never have known that. I'll tell Mum to dig hers out now.

journey.section: How do guests get to Bali and between the areas?
journey.quote: Does the venue arrange guest transport, and for how many guests?
journey.reaction: Good questions, but none about a guest who can't climb into a minibus or manage steps. There's no accessibility question anywhere on the list.

journey.section: When is the right time to get married in Bali?
journey.quote: There have been cases of methanol poisoning in Bali, so serve and order only branded alcohol.
journey.reaction: Frightening, but I'm glad it's there. Practical and specific.

journey.section: When is the right time to get married in Bali?
journey.quote: Rabies is found throughout Indonesia, and dengue occurs in Bali, so guests should check vaccinations before travel.
journey.reaction: Fine, but where is travel insurance? With volcanoes, flight cancellations and older guests, I expected a line about proper cover including medical evacuation.

journey.section: When is the right time to get married in Bali?
journey.quote: Know your venue's emergency plans, and keep the local emergency numbers to hand: ambulance and rescue 118, police 110 or 112.
journey.reaction: Useful, but I'd rather know who from your side I ring at 2am Bali time if something goes wrong. That's the number I want.

journey.section: Can foreigners legally marry in Bali?
journey.quote: Persons of any nationality may generally marry in Indonesia if they hold a religion recognised by the Indonesian Government, listed as Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism or Christian, and both parties must hold the same religion.
journey.reaction: Same religion? Our daughter isn't religious and her fiance certainly isn't. Does that mean it has to be done at home first? It's clear, but it's worrying and it doesn't say what most couples do.

journey.section: Shortlist your Bali venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person, AUD, our time zone. Exactly what I want. I'd still want their name and a phone call.

journey.section: Shortlist your Bali venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing first and they handle payments. That's someone accountable. But are the payments protected if a Bali supplier goes under?

unanswered_questions: Are our deposits protected if a Bali venue or supplier fails, and whose name is on the contract? (deferred business detail)
Who do we ring if something goes wrong in Bali after hours? Is anyone from Wedded Wonderland there on the day? (deferred business detail)
Which of these venues have step-free access or buggies between the ceremony and dinner spaces, for a guest with a walking frame?
Should guests take out travel insurance with medical evacuation cover, and do you advise on it?
Roughly what does a Bali wedding at these venues cost, From AUD?
If the couple don't share a recognised religion, what do most Australians do: marry legally at home and have a blessing in Bali?
Do you arrange guest airport transfers, including for elderly guests? (deferred business detail)
How is your fee charged, and do you take commissions from venues? (deferred business detail)
Is the first conversation a phone call with a real person, and can I join it as a parent paying part?

turn_offs_found.quote: Site visits are by appointment, and whether a minimum spend or rental fee applies depends on the space and the type of event.
turn_offs_found.why: The page never mentions deposits, contracts in rupiah or what happens to our money. My card says that's a turn-off, and with this much money going in, it's the first thing I look for.

turn_offs_found.quote: Not published: room count, exclusive use.
turn_offs_found.why: Fifteen venues, each with four bullets, and this line again and again. On the iPad it becomes a long grey block. I lost track of which venue was which by Nusa Dua.

turn_offs_found.quote: Australians have drowned in rough seas and rip currents at popular beaches, including in Bali.
turn_offs_found.why: Not a tone problem; it's calm and correct. But the beach venues are presented happily above it, and the warning is left with nothing about who keeps the family safe or what insurance they need.

would_share_with: My husband, the key takeaways, the 'confirms inclusions in writing before you sign' line and the closing paragraph about the fee in writing and AUD quotes
My mother, the passport damage line and the vaccinations line, so she gets organised early
My daughter, the religion requirement in the legal section, so she checks it before anyone books anything

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
cta_reaction.why: The right words: one person, AUD, fee in writing. Bali feels manageable after this, but I'd talk to Geoff first and I'd want a phone call with a real person who can tell me how deposits are protected, who we ring on the day, and whether Mum can actually reach the chapel.

top_3_changes: Add one line on deposits and contracts (whose name, what currency, when money becomes non-refundable) as a question to ask each venue, plus what Wedded Concierge does about payments, only if the business confirms it; otherwise flag it.

Add an accessibility question to the transport checklist (step-free routes, buggies between ceremony and dinner spaces) and a travel insurance line with medical evacuation cover in the safety section, sourced from Smartraveller.
Break up the 15 venue sections for easier reading on a tablet, for example a one-line 'best for' summary under each venue name, so the repeated 'Not published' lines don't blur together.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on deposits, who is responsible, elderly guests, safety, insurance and a phone call
No invented brand facts; deposit protection, on-the-day contact, transfers, fees and accessibility placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Can the business confirm what Wedded Concierge does about deposits, payments and on-the-day contact in Bali, so one reassuring line can be added? If not, flag rather than fill.

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing about half. Relevance is 3 because a venue list is written for the couple, though it covers travel, health and the legal position.
Clarity is 4: well ordered with a jump list and tables, but the length of the venue section tires her.

Likelihood to enquire is 3: AUD and fee-in-writing earn trust, but deposits, insurance and accessibility are not addressed. Missing on-the-day help is a deferred business detail, not penalised as must-fix.
Her mother's walking frame comes from the persona card; husband's name (Geoff) is character colour consistent with earlier panels, not a page fact.
Fast mode: full article read top to bottom, venue sections partly skimmed as she would, FAQ skimmed as it repeats the body.
